grammarFocus: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.

title: Comparing Environmental Monitoring Methods: A Community Science Project
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数。请先听/读对话，完成10道听力题；然后学习语法讲解，完成8道语法题；最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。听力部分包含自然对话、修正和干扰信息，答案不会直接读出。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
transcript:
Mia: Hi, Tom. Thanks for meeting me. I'm planning the community air-quality project for our neighborhood. We need to choose a monitoring method. Can you help me compare options?
Tom: Sure, Mia. I read about three methods: low-cost sensors, official monitoring stations, and citizen science kits. Each has strengths and weaknesses.
Mia: Let's start with low-cost sensors. They are cheap, so we can buy many. But are they accurate?
Tom: They are less accurate than official stations. However, if we use many sensors, we can see patterns across the neighborhood. The main problem is that they need regular calibration.
Mia: Right. Calibration takes time. What about official stations?
Tom: Official stations are very accurate. They are the gold standard. But they are expensive, and there are only two in our city. So we can't get detailed local data.
Mia: That's a big limitation. Citizen science kits might be a good middle ground. They are cheaper than official stations but more accurate than low-cost sensors.
Tom: Yes, but they depend on volunteers. If volunteers collect data consistently, the kits work well. If not, data quality suffers.
Mia: So the kits are reliable only if people are committed. Hmm. We also need to think about funding. The city may give us a small grant, but it might not be enough for official stations.
Tom: Exactly. We can apply for the grant, but we can't rely on it. Low-cost sensors are within our budget even without the grant.
Mia: True. But if we choose low-cost sensors, we must train volunteers to calibrate them. That could be a challenge.
Tom: Maybe we can combine methods. Use a few citizen science kits for accurate local readings, and many low-cost sensors for wide coverage. Although it's more complex, it might give us the best picture.
Mia: That's an interesting idea. But managing two systems might be too difficult for our small team.
Tom: You're right. We should consider our capacity. We have only five volunteers. So maybe we should start simple.
Mia: Let's think about the goal. We want to identify pollution hotspots. For that, wide coverage is more important than perfect accuracy. So low-cost sensors might be sufficient.
Tom: I agree. But we should still validate the sensor data with a few citizen science kits. That way, we can check the sensors' accuracy.
Mia: Good point. So the plan: buy twenty low-cost sensors, and use two citizen science kits for validation. We can apply for the grant to cover the kits.
Tom: That sounds practical. Even if the grant doesn't come through, we can still buy the sensors. The kits are optional.
Mia: Perfect. I'll write the proposal. Thanks for your help, Tom.
Tom: You're welcome. Let me know if you need more information.

grammar.title: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，我们可以用从句表达原因、结果和让步。原因常用 because, since, as；结果常用 so, so that；让步常用 although, even though, even if。注意：although/even though 不能和 but 同时使用。may / might / can 表示可能性时语气不同：can 表示一般能力或客观可能；may 表示较正式的可能性；might 表示可能性较小或更不确定。例如：We can buy sensors.（我们有能力买）The city may give us a grant.（可能给，较正式）It might not be enough.（可能不够，不确定性更大）。
grammar.example: Even if the grant doesn't come through, we can still buy the sensors.

questions.prompt: _____ low-cost sensors are cheap, they need regular calibration.
questions.explanation: 句子表示让步：虽然传感器便宜，但需要校准。Although 引导让步从句。
questions.evidence: Although it's more complex, it might give us the best picture.

questions.prompt: The team has only five volunteers, _____ they cannot manage two systems.
questions.explanation: 前半句是原因，后半句是结果，用 so 连接。
questions.evidence: We have only five volunteers. So maybe we should start simple.

questions.prompt: We should validate the data with kits _____ we can check the sensors' accuracy.
questions.explanation: so that 引导目的/结果从句，表示“以便”。
questions.evidence: That way, we can check the sensors' accuracy.

questions.prompt: The city _____ give us a grant, but it is not certain.
questions.explanation: may 表示较正式的可能性，不确定。
questions.evidence: The city may give us a small grant.

questions.prompt: We _____ apply for the grant, but we can't rely on it.
questions.explanation: can 表示能力或客观可能，这里表示“我们可以申请”。
questions.evidence: We can apply for the grant, but we can't rely on it.

questions.prompt: The grant _____ not be enough for official stations. (less certain)
questions.explanation: might 表示可能性较小或更不确定。
questions.evidence: it might not be enough for official stations.

questions.prompt: _____ we use many sensors, we can see patterns across the neighborhood.
questions.explanation: 条件从句用 if 引导。
questions.evidence: if we use many sensors, we can see patterns across the neighborhood.

questions.prompt: Citizen science kits are more accurate than low-cost sensors, _____ they depend on volunteers.
questions.explanation: 前后为转折关系，用 but 连接。
questions.evidence: They are cheaper than official stations but more accurate than low-cost sensors.
